# Requirements Document: Order items and orders

## Introduction

Order items hold services and carry the price; an order holds order items.
The statuses of items and orders follow from their services, as the ONE Order
implementation guide defines them.

These requirements are generated from the Lean model in [`Rules/OneOrder/Order.lean`](https://github.com/samdengler/verified-air/blob/main/Rules/OneOrder/Order.lean). Each acceptance criterion carries the status the build computed for it: *proven* means a theorem the build checked, *example only* means a computed example, *open* means a theorem the build could not prove, and *not checked* means no theorem or example covers it yet.

## Requirements

### Requirement ONE-002

**User Story:** As a revenue accountant, I want each order item's status worked out from its services, so that I know which items still hold value.

**Rule:** THE SYSTEM SHALL give each order item the status active, cancelled or closed from the service and delivery statuses of its services. (Lean: `itemStatuses`)

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHILE at least one service of an order item holds value THE SYSTEM SHALL mark the item active.
   - ONE-002.1, proven: proven theorem `item_active_iff`; example `paidItem`
2. WHEN every service of an order item is cancelled or transferred and none holds value THE SYSTEM SHALL mark the item cancelled.
   - ONE-002.2, proven: proven theorem `item_cancelled_iff`; example `cancelledItem`
3. WHEN at least one service of an order item is delivered and every other service is delivered or removed THE SYSTEM SHALL mark the item closed.
   - ONE-002.3, proven: proven theorem `item_closed_iff`; example `closedItem`
4. THE SYSTEM SHALL give each order item exactly one status.
   - ONE-002.4, open: proven theorem `active_not_cancelled`; proven theorem `active_not_closed`; open theorem `item_has_one_status`; counterexample `unpaidCancellationWhileRequested`; counterexample `deliveredThenTransferred`; counterexample `suspendedService`

#### Open question on ONE-002.4

> Each order item has exactly one status, active, cancelled or closed.
>
> Open question for the business.  The guide's three conditions overlap and
> leave gaps.  An item whose one service was delivered and then transferred to
> another item meets both the cancelled condition \(every service transferred,
> none holding value\) and the closed condition \(a service delivered, the rest
> delivered or removed\).  The example `deliveredThenTransferred` shows it.
> Which status wins, and should a delivered service be transferable at all?

### Requirement ONE-003

**User Story:** As an airline, I want an order's status worked out from its items and services, so that an order is closed only when nothing in it holds value.

**Rule:** THE SYSTEM SHALL mark an order opened while any of its services holds value, and closed once all its items are closed or cancelled and all its services are delivered or removed. (Lean: `orderStatuses`)

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHILE at least one service of an order holds value THE SYSTEM SHALL mark the order opened.
   - ONE-003.1, proven: proven theorem `order_opened_iff`; example `acceptFamilyOffer`
2. WHEN every item of an order is closed or cancelled and every service is delivered or removed THE SYSTEM SHALL mark the order closed.
   - ONE-003.2, proven: proven theorem `order_closed_iff`; example `deliveredOrder`
3. THE SYSTEM SHALL never mark an order both opened and closed.
   - ONE-003.3, proven: proven theorem `opened_closed_exclusive`
4. THE SYSTEM SHALL give every order that has a service either the status opened or the status closed.
   - ONE-003.4, open: open theorem `order_opened_or_closed`; counterexample `expiredService`

#### Open question on ONE-003.4

> Every order with at least one service is opened or closed.
>
> Open question for the business.  The guide closes an order only when every
> service is delivered or removed, and keeps it opened only while a service
> holds value.  It does not say whether an expired, not claimed or failed
> service holds value.  Under a reading where an expired service holds none, an
> order whose only service expired is neither opened nor closed.  The example
> `expiredService` shows it.  Does an expired service hold value, and
> should an order with one be closed?
